conventions: κύριον τὸν θεόν σου (4:7, 4:10): the supplied *the* belongs to the anarthrous κύριον as a rule 7 helper (rule 51's anarthrous clause), σου takes the determiner slot of θεόν with *thy*, and the article τόν is `unrepresented` under rule 20. Both verses read the collocation this way. Do not hand the *the* to the article standing before θεόν: the English determiner stands in front of κύριον, which has no article of its own.

The chapter marks nothing `added`; every ASV-supplied word was traced to a token that licenses it. The two asterisked supplies are the decisive ones. At 4:21 *son* goes into the governing article's own phrase under rule 102, so τὸν τοῦ Ζεβεδαίου gives *the son* to τόν headed on *son*, leaves the inner τοῦ `unrepresented` under rule 21's determinerless clause, and gives *of Zebedee* to the name; reading *the son of* whole on the outer article under rule 52's genealogical arm remains defensible. At 4:25 the repeated *from* is a rule 7 helper on πέραν under rule 103's repeated-function-word clause, the single ἀπό governing both coordinate members.

A particle standing with a compound verb rides inside that verb's own unit wherever no expressed preposition governs the phrase — 4:1 *was led up*, 4:12 *was delivered up*, 4:16 *did spring up*, 4:21 *going on*, 4:23 *went about*, 4:24 *went forth* — and is headed on the verb word (rule 106). At 4:4 an expressed διά does govern the phrase, so the whole English prepositional expression *out of* is the preposition's under rule 36 and ἐκπορευομένῳ keeps a bare *proceedeth*; leaving διά a bare *of* while the verb took *out* is what rule 106 forbids. The two treatments are one analysis and not a split.

τότε is *Then* on its own at 4:5, 4:10 and 4:11, and splits at 4:17, where the expressed ἀπό takes *From* and τότε takes *that time*: the ASV wrote separate English words, so rule 94's count test forbids a compound unit. The head is *time*, the word answering to the adverb's temporal core under rule 66; heading it on *that* as the deictic element remains defensible. The difference between the two renderings is licensed by the Greek and is not a cross-verse split.
report: Read all 25 verses end to end and worked through every one of the 35 candidate lemma groups. No construction is analysed two ways with nothing in the source or in the ASV's own wording to license the difference, so no patch is returned.

Article audit (65 tokens, 9 nominal treatments): the nine genitive article+noun pairs divide cleanly on rule 21's determiner test — aligned to *of the* where the ASV writes a determiner (4:5 τοῦ ἱεροῦ, 4:8 τοῦ κόσμου, 4:15 τῶν ἐθνῶν, 4:23 τῆς βασιλείας) and `unrepresented` with the case preposition on the noun where it does not (4:3, 4:6 τοῦ θεοῦ → *of God*; 4:17 τῶν οὐρανῶν → *of heaven*; 4:18 τῆς Γαλιλαίας; 4:21 τοῦ Ζεβεδαίου). Ten articles before names or place names are `unrepresented` throughout (4:1, 4:7, 4:10, 4:12, 4:13, 4:17, 4:23 ×2, 4:24, 4:25). Three lemmas' worth of articles are emptied by a possessive under rule 20 (σου at 4:6, 4:7, 4:10; αὐτοῦ/αὐτῶν at 4:18, 4:21 ×3, 4:22, 4:23) and one by a demonstrative under rule 38 (4:3 οἱ … οὗτοι).

Substantival articles before participles are consistent and divide by the count of English words the ASV wrote, exactly as rules 32 and 90 require: 4:3 ὁ πειράζων → *the* / *tempter*; 4:14 τὸ ῥηθέν → *which* / *was spoken*; 4:16 τοῖς καθημένοις → *to them* / *that sat*; 4:24 τοὺς … ἔχοντας → *that* / *were*. The two second-attributive articles (4:16 ὁ καθήμενος, 4:18 τὸν λεγόμενον) are `unrepresented` under rule 31 and rule 32's apposition clause, and 4:13's post-nominal τήν keeps only *which*. That is one analysis, not five.

The candidate table is blind to `added` units, so I audited every ASV-supplied word directly. The chapter carries no `added` unit and none is owed: supplied determiners go to anarthrous nouns (4:3, 4:6, 4:7, 4:10, 4:13, 4:15 ×3, 4:16), supplied subjects and copulas to their verbs or predicates, supplied clause junctures to the clause they introduce (4:3, 4:4, 4:9, 4:13, 4:20, 4:22), *ye* to the imperatives at 4:17 and 4:19, expletive *there* to ἠκολούθησαν at 4:25, and the two asterisked supplies — *son* at 4:21 and *from* at 4:25 — to the article and to πέραν under rules 102 and 103. No fold-versus-add split hides behind the clean table.

Verb-particle handling is uniform: the particle rides inside the compound verb's unit at 4:1 *led up*, 4:12 *delivered up*, 4:16 *spring up*, 4:21 *going on*, 4:23 *went about*, 4:24 *went forth*, and the single apparent exception at 4:4 is licensed by an expressed διά governing the phrase, which takes *out of* whole under rule 36. Logged as a convention so it is not later mistaken for a split.

BSB: the one disagreement, MAT.4.17 τῶν (*of the*, ASV `unrepresented` / BSB represented), is a documented convention difference and not an error. The ASV writes *the kingdom of heaven* with no determiner on *heaven*, so rule 21's determinerless clause and rule 23 leave the article nothing to anchor and keep *of* with the noun — the same test the chapter applies to the other eight genitive articles. Changing it would contradict the contract to improve an aggregate the report itself says is not a quality score.

Head hedges left standing, each with its competing reading already in the unit's note: τότε → *that time* headed on *time* (4:17), δαιμονιζομένους → *possessed with demons* headed on *demons* (4:24, rules 66 and 91's denominal arm), and the split of κακῶς ἔχοντας into *sick* and *were* (4:24, rule 2 against rule 73's collapse arm). None is a cross-verse matter and none warrants a patch.

Conventions: none had been recorded, and the validator counted 39 note strings repeating across verses. Four chapter-wide judgments are recorded now; the remaining repetitions are bare form labels (*Noun.*, *Adverb.*, *Connective.*) or verbatim restatements of rules 19, 20, 21, 23, 51 and 88, which already bind every verse and would only bury the four that matter.

Promotions: none. The chapter met no case the contract had not considered — rules 21, 31, 32, 36, 51, 90, 94, 102, 103 and 106 each decided their construction as written, and the two places where the wording is thin (rule 57's inner article with a determinerless possessor, rule 106's arm where the preverb and the expressed preposition are different lexemes) are already decided by rules 21 and 36 in terms, so an amendment there would be a restatement with a new address.
